VEHICLE HIRING BID CONDITIONS 1 Vehicle should be registered in the name of Tenderer and should not sublet a ny part of the contract. a) Bidders can submit the EMD with 2% of the estimated cost of services, in the forms of DD/FDR/ Banker Cheque in favour of SR.DIVISIONAL FINANCE MANAGER/GUNTAKAL p ayable at SR.DIVISIONAL FINANCE MANAGER/GUNTAKAL. Hardcopy to the Buyer to be s ubmitted within 5 days of Bid End date / Bid Opening date. b) Successful bidder has to deposit Performance guarantee/PBG to the tune of 10 % of the contractual value, which shall be returned to the contractor after successful compl etion of contract. This PG has to be submitted within 30 days from date of issue of con tract to the CMS/RH/GTL. Successful Bidder can submit the Performance guarantee/PBG in the form of DD/Fixed Deposit Receipt (FDR). FDR/DD should be made out or pledged in the Favour of Sr.DFM/SCOR RLY/GTL on A/C (Name of the Agency). For release of Performance guarantee/PBG, the FDR/DD will be released in favour of bidder by the CMS/RH/GTL Under MSE category, only Service Providers for Services tendered are eligible for Exemption from EMD. Railway jurisdiction), valid insurance and should me et requirements of pollution standard etc. as per provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and fulfil any oth er statutory obligations as applicable including all safety approved accessories/ equipment fitted t o the vehicle. This should be ensured by the CMS/RH/GTL 5 The vehicle proposed to be offered on hire should be in good condition and not more than 4 year s old, on the date of opening of tender. 6 The vehicle should be mechanically sound and shall be well maintained with neat and clean inter iors/exteriors. The driver should display good behavior and be neatly dressed. Smoking and use of cell phone during driving by Driver is prohibited. It is desirable that driver should wear proper neat and clean formal uniform with shoes. 7 The contractor/agency participating in the tender should normally be GST compliant regarding re gistration, filing of returns etc., and shall be fully responsible for the compliance as per GST Act at all times. If the Contractor falls either “below the turnover threshold for GST” or is a “Composition Taxable Person” under the CGST Act, a self-declaration should be enclosed with his offer duly supp orted by a certificate of turnover from a Chartered Accountant or enclose Form „REG-06‟ showing as “Composition” under Type of Registration and no GST is applicable for contracts with such pers ons/firms. Scope of Service: The Scope of service deals with hiring of all-inclusive monthly basis Ambulance service ( including all expenses towards running of ambulance such as, but not l imited to drivers salary, fuel requirements, maintenance, taxes and other expenses) of a Type D - Advanced Life Support Ambulance that run on either pe trol or diesel, which are specially equipped and ergonomically designed for tran sportation / emergent treatment of sick or injured people and capable of providi ng out of hospital medical care during transit / when stationary, commensurate

with its designated level of care when appropriately staffed. The duration of hire would be 24 months on 7 days a week and 24 hours basis. The ambulances provided should be CMVR approved and Automotive Industry S tandards – 125 (Part 1 & 2) compliant, Category M 4-wheeler vehicle, ergonomi cally designed, suitably equipped and appropriately staffed for the transport an d treatment of emergency patients requiring invasive airway management/ inte nsive monitoring. Services for which hired ambulance will be used at DRH/GTL: 1· Attending emergency calls from Employees at work place like DRM Office, ot her departmental Offices, Diesel shed, Railway station, open lines and around G untakal Town 2· Attending emergency calls of Railway beneficiaries within Railway colonies an d Guntakal town limits and transferring patient to DRH/GTL 3· Transport of Inpatient’s for any investigations/professional consultations withi n Guntakal town limits 4· Attending passenger train calls by medical team and if required for shifting p assengers to DRH/GTL or Government Hospital in case of serious illness5· For tr ansport of medical team, equipment’s & necessary furniture for conducting cam ps by Health & Family welfare department6· For transport of medical equipment’s, medicines which are received at courier/transport office 7· Transport of outstation patients to Railway station 8· Transport of patients referred to empanelled hospitals at Kurnool (130Kms) or Anantapur (85Kms) or any other higher centre 9· To attend Train accident relief services 10· To arrange first aid and as standby medical services at various Railway Prog rammes 11· To accompany VIP visits 12· All activities relating to Medical Department of Guntakal Division 13· Any activity of medical department on instructions of CMS/In-charge Medical Officer 14· To provide relief ambulance services at other health units of GTL division if necessity arises. Service Details and Standards: 1. Proposed ambulance should be Single stretcher premium van of make similar to Tata Winger Ambulance 3200/3400 or Force Traveller Ambulance or SML Isuz u Ambulance or Tata 407 Ambulance or of similar make with manufacture year 2024 or after with travelled up to 50,000Kms.

2. Ambulance deployed should confirm to the specifications with all-requisite fac tory fitted accessories, tools, and accessories including spare wheels and the ot her equipment in compliance as per AIS-125 of the National Ambulance Code a nd as per the M.V.Act /Rules in force. The ambulance should preferably be of wh ite colour. 3. Constructional and Functional Requirements for Road Ambulance should be as per AIS-125 (Part-1) of the National Ambulance Code and technical requirement s for medical equipment should be as per AIS-125 (Part-2) of the National Ambul ance Code and over that, specifications mentioned in this document. Other ter ms and conditions mentioned in Service level agreement for Monthly basis amb ulance service in GeM are also applicable. 4. Ambulance deployed shall have all the necessary permits/licenses/clearances such as, but not limited to fitness certificate, PUC, full comprehensive insurance (including third party, property and damage coverage),road permit, registration certificate as per the Motor Vehicles Act, RTO and other applicable laws and sta tutory bodies, for providing commercial vehicles for this service and should be r egistered with Transport department of Andhra Pradesh. 5. Ambulance should be in excellent working condition (both internally and exter nally) at all times and should be cleaned thoroughly both internally and externa lly, boot kept clear of dust, rubbish, oil, bad odor and any personal belongings o f the driver. 6. The ambulance should ensure: a) minimum noise of engine and body while running b) tires with proper treads c) appropriately inflated stepney d) working headlights, tail lamps, indicators, speedometer, milometer etc. e) proper paint on the outside f) good condition of bumpers g) upholstery in good condition including washed and ironed white seat covers h) proper locking of all doors i) proper closing and opening of all windows. 7. Ambulance shall be available 24-hours of everyday in the week including Sun day parked at the Casualty or premises of DRH/Guntakal with full or sufficient ta nk of fuel availability. 8. In case the vehicle is not available due to any reason, the contractor must pro vide another vehicle with similar model & facility and any low facility arrangeme nts will not be acceptable. 9. In case of non-availability of the vehicle the CMS/GTL may arrange another ve hicle and the expenditure incurred in this way would be recovered from the mo nthly bill of the tenderer /bidder including initiating proper action.

10. In case of noncompliance of the standards of the services to be provided as p er this agreement, CMS GTL would be at liberty to levy such penalty and termin ate the contract as per the conditions detailed out in SLA of GeM. 11. Ambulances deployed cannot be taken-out of DRH/GTL without written per mission from CMS/GTL or nominated In-charge Medical Officer. 12. The front and rear wind screens should have a sticker reading “AMBULANC E”. The Ambulance shall display a mark “ON SOUTH COAST RAILWAY DUTY” on the ambulance at his cost, for making the ambulance conspicuously distinguishable from a distance. 13. Any expenditure towards of wear and tear, repairing or regular servicing and maintenance would be borne by the tenderer/bidder. 14. Hospital shall not be liable for any damage to vehicle during the course of use. 15. The legal liability arising out of Accident (whether on duty or off duty) if any, during the period of engagement would be managed and borne by the tenderer /bidder. 16. Any loss of property or any other claim caused by the driver would be recove red from the monthly bill of the tenderer/bidder. 17. The driver employed by the bidder should be under insurance cover of accid ent policy for loss of life/injury etc and compensation, if any this regard if award ed, will be the responsibility of the bidder. 18. The ambulance must have a dedicated working smart mobile connection for easy contact by Doctor’s, hospital staff or passengers. It must also have an acti ve internet connection at all times where google maps can be accessed, to navi gate the shortest and/ or fastest route possible avoiding traffic jams. The driver on duty shall be reachable at all times through this mobile number. The driver s hould be sharing the live location by any means available when demanded by t he hospital authority 19. Payment of all applicable statutory obligations such as minimum wages lab our laws, tax laws etc. Rules are to be observed by the tenderer & hence all sta tuary liability viz. ESI/EPF etc would be solely borne by the tenderer/bidder and no extra payment would be made on these account. 20. Format of Log Book is in Annexure-I. 21. Patient cabin of the Ambulance should have following features : a) Patient cabin heated, ventilated, and air conditioned as required in accordan ce with the criteria specified in AIS-125 (Part-1) of the National Ambulance Code b) Vehicle should have reinforced suspension system for providing to patient a Comfortable ride, free from external noise.

c) Adequate power supply arrangements for medical equipment’s. d) Adequate patient cabin space for patient (In comfortable position),and seat f or at – least one attendant and two paramedics amendable for attending to the patient. e) Complete flooring free of joints suitable for easy cleaning/scientific/ fumigatio n and treatment with disinfectants. f) Two (at least) superior quality fans and sufficient lighting arrangements and e xhaust fan. g) Storage space for keeping medical equipment’s and consumables required. h) Siren and beacon as per approved norms of govt. i) A “No Smoking” sign will be prominently displayed in the patient compartmen t. 22.List of Equipment to be made available in the Ambulance : a) Patient Handling Equipment 1. Portable Suction Aspirator, Manual – 1 Nos d) Type of Diagnostic Equipment: 1. Manual B. P. Monitor Cuff Size: 10 cm. - 66 cm – 1 Nos 2. Pulse Oximeter– 1 Nos 3. Stethoscope– 1 Nos 4. Fire Extinguisher, ABC Type (minimum 2 kg capacity complying with IS:13849 or IS:2171) 10. Nebulisation Device – 1 Nos 23. DRIVERS: a) The drivers of the ambulances must possess a valid driver license and must have a minimum 2 years of driving experience. b) The Drivers should have the basic knowledge on First Aid and ABC resuscitation in case of medical emergencies. c) The drivers of the ambulance deployed should maintain polite & courteous b ehaviour towards the Hospital staff/ passenger. “Misbehaviour” which may inclu de, but not limited to, consumption of alcohol during d by user, use of abusive l anguage, uncordial behaviour, theft, shall attract penalties as per provisions of t he contract. d) The Driver shall remain available all the times as per Duty Roster and shall n ot leave place of Duty from assigned Ambulances without prior permission of Ho spital authority. e) The driver should update about the trip status when demanded while in journ ey.

The contractor must avoid frequent employment of new staf f and if any deficiency in quality of service due to frequent change of staff is noticed, CMS/GTL may levy penalty of Rs.5000 per instance. 31. Cleanliness and sanitisation of Ambulance is the responsibility of tenderer/bi dder as per National Guidelines for Clean Hospitals by MoH&FW. As per point No:6.9 of the s aid guidelines, Ambulances should be cleaned by following below mentioned principles: a) Routine clean following each transport: 1. Place biomedical waste (e.g., dressings, bandages, contaminated sheets that are saturated with blood) in a colour coded bins as per Biomedical Waste (Management and Handling) Rules 1998. 2.
